clue.text: Disinterested like Bill Brewer and Co

blocks.note: first meaning: impartial, taking no side
second meaning, read cryptically: in the folk song 'Widecombe Fair', Bill Brewer, Jan Stewer and the rest are set on going to the fair

explanation.surface: Someone is praised for being as impartial as a band of old West Country villagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Widecombe Fair' is a Devon folk song whose chorus lists Bill Brewer, Jan Stewer, Peter Gurney and Uncle Tom Cobley and all, riding to the fair; split the answer and they were minded for the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterested properly means impartial, without personal stake, which is exactly what a just and unbiased person is.

clue.text: Commons passenger?

blocks.note: first meaning: commons is food provided for a community, as at a college table
second meaning: a paying traveller in a taxi or bus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Commons' suggests the House of Commons; here it is the old word for shared rations.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is food served at a meal, the sense of commons, and also a person who pays to ride in a cab.

clue.text: Take up oriental dress for Queen's attendant

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the sari is the draped garment worn by women in South Asia

explanation.surface: An instruction to shorten an Eastern garment for a royal lady-in-waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen is Cleopatra: in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra, Iras and Charmian are her waiting-women.
explanation.definitionFit: Iras is one of the serving women who attend Cleopatra, Egypt's queen, in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: In which shooting stars excel

blocks.note: surface reading: an astronomy note about where meteors shine brightest
setter's reading: star performers at shooting, crack shots on the range, and the skill they excel in

explanation.surface: A line about the region of sky where meteors are most dazzling.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill with a rifle or gun is the craft at which the best shots, the stars of shooting, are superior.

clue.text: Music of the Muses?

blocks.note: surface reading: the songs the goddesses of the arts inspire
setter's reading: there are nine Muses, so their music would be a piece for nine players

explanation.surface: A wondering question about what the goddesses of inspiration might sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for nine performers suits a group of nine goddesses performing together.

clue.text: Observe advocate of free trade in the plant

blocks.note: to eye something is to watch it
John Bright, Victorian politician who campaigned against the Corn Laws for free trade

explanation.surface: Someone is told to spot a free-trade campaigner hidden in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory or a planted spy; it is a flower. John Bright and Richard Cobden led the Anti-Corn Law League.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower, Euphrasia, once used as a herbal remedy for sore eyes.

clue.text: Stop and throw

blocks.note: first meaning: a stopper for a cask, or to plug a hole
second meaning: British slang for tossing something casually

explanation.walkthrough: To bung something over is British informal speech for chucking it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung plugs the hole in a barrel, and in casual British speech to bung is to toss carelessly.

clue.text: Rota unduly complicated — how like the war-time navy of the RNVR!

definitions.text: how like the war-time navy of the RNVR!

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters before it come out in a muddled order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that a duty roster is muddled, likened to the wartime volunteer navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The RNVR (Royal Naval Volunteer Reserve) wore wavy gold braid on their sleeves and were nicknamed the Wavy Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Undulatory means wavy, rising and falling, which matches the nickname given to the reserve whose rank stripes rippled.

clue.text: It's on track for easy money in the USA

definitions.text: It's on track for easy money in the USA

blocks.note: surface reading: something heading the right way toward easy riches

blocks.clueFragment: It's on track for easy money in the USA
blocks.note: setter's reading: a literal train running on rails, whose cargo is the American slang for money got without effort

explanation.surface: A scheme is said to be heading for quick profits in America.
explanation.walkthrough: In American slang gravy is unearned money, so a train carrying it on the track is the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a job or scheme that yields large rewards for little effort, originally American slang.

clue.text: This American bird a jogger?

blocks.note: the straight half: a long-tailed cuckoo of the American deserts that sprints on foot
setter's reading: someone who runs along the streets for exercise

explanation.surface: A playful question whether a certain American bird takes runs for fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is a ground cuckoo of the south-western United States, famous for running rather than flying.

clue.text: Paragon without Latin? Just a thought!

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following item is removed from the word

blocks.note: a paragon is a perfect example, a model
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a model of perfection without Latin is only a passing notion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion that occurs to the mind, a thought put forward tentatively.

clue.text: Upon reflection it shows the way to bat

definitions.text: Upon reflection it shows the way to bat

blocks.clueFragment: Upon reflection it shows the way to bat
blocks.note: surface reading: a cricket coach, after some thought, demonstrating how to hold the willow
setter's reading: sound bouncing back off objects guides the flying mammal through the dark

explanation.surface: After due consideration, someone demonstrates batting technique, as in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upon reflection' looks like 'after thinking'; it is literal reflected sound, and the bat is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats navigate by emitting calls and reading the returning sound, a sonar-like method of locating obstacles and prey.

clue.text: Secretly convert a cloister in Ely

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: An order to quietly turn a cathedral cloister in Ely to new use.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterically describes doing something in a manner understood only by an initiated few, hence privately or secretly.

clue.text: “Misery acquaints a man with strange " (Tempest)

blocks.note: the quotation with its last word missing; the solver supplies it
the source: Trinculo says this in Shakespeare's The Tempest when he shelters under Caliban's cloak

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank from The Tempest, Act 2: Trinculo crawls under Caliban's gaberdine to escape a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means people sharing a bed, and by extension unlikely partners thrown together by circumstance.

clue.text: Their's the first two places in the race

definitions.text: Their's the first two places in the race

blocks.clueFragment: the first two places in the race
blocks.note: surface reading: the winner and runner-up of a sporting contest
setter's reading: the human race, whose first two members came before everyone else

explanation.surface: A sports commentator noting which pair claimed the top two finishing positions.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the earliest man and woman were created first, so they hold the opening places of humankind.

clue.text: Engaging organ to take part in finale

indicators.note: taking part in something means going inside it, so the first item sits within the second

blocks.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a finale is the conclusion of a piece

explanation.surface: An appealing instrument, perhaps a church organ, joins in a grand closing number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging and endearing both describe someone charming who wins affection and attracts people.

clue.text: Rash? Cheeky? That's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one item wraps around the other

blocks.note: cheeky and impudent both mean disrespectfully bold
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether calling behaviour reckless or saucy is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash and imprudent both describe acting without proper caution or regard for consequences.

clue.text: This space for those less skilled in 3

definitions.note: the answer qualifies 'space', as in the phrase for the cosmos beyond Earth
the target ring where poorer shots land

blocks.note: first meaning: the vast region beyond the atmosphere, named with this adjective
second meaning: 3 is the shooting clue, and the outermost ring of a target is where weaker marksmen hit, scoring least

explanation.surface: A notice reserving an area for the less proficient competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer qualifies the cosmos beyond our planet, and also names the lowest-scoring ring on an archery or rifle target.

clue.text: Shows high dudgeon making no end of fuss about yours truly

indicators.note: no end of means without its last letter, so the final letter is cut off
about means going around, so the shortened word wraps around the next item

blocks.note: taken as written
yours truly is a jocular way of saying 'me', the writer

explanation.surface: Someone shows great indignation by creating endless commotion over the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is the setter's jokey way of referring to themself, a common crossword route to the first-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: To fume is to seethe with anger, which is what showing high dudgeon, deep resentment, amounts to.

clue.text: Vessel to dispense tea to Royal Institution, fragrant mixture

blocks.note: a pot is a container
you pour tea when serving it
RI is the abbreviation for the Royal Institution, the London science body

explanation.surface: A teapot used to serve tea at a learned London society, with a sweet scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot-pourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept for its pleasant scent, a perfumed blend.

clue.text: Describing degrees of difference between East and West

definitions.text: Describing degrees of difference between East and West

blocks.clueFragment: degrees of difference between East and West
blocks.note: surface reading: how far apart Eastern and Western cultures or politics are
setter's reading: the angular measure on a map counting how far a place lies east or west of Greenwich

explanation.surface: A commentator measuring the gulf between Eastern and Western blocs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East and West' suggests Cold War politics; it is the globe's meridians.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective concerns longitude, the angular position measured east or west of the prime meridian.

clue.text: Losing hazard at home and away?

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A sports page note that a risk to defeat exists in both home and away games.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards, a losing hazard is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball; players call it an in-off.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards the term names the stroke where your own ball drops into a pocket after striking another, scoring as a losing hazard.

clue.text: Endure stars little and great

definitions.note: two constellations, the Little and Great one

blocks.note: first meaning: put up with, tolerate
second meaning: the constellations Ursa Minor and Ursa Major share this name

explanation.surface: Someone must put up with celebrities both minor and major.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to tolerate hardship, and the Great and Little Bear are the northern constellations Ursa Major and Minor.

clue.text: Sainted historian — one told by a priest, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that what follows is judged by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: to tell beads is to count prayers on a rosary, so each is one told by a priest

explanation.surface: A saintly chronicler is described as a man whose story a cleric once recounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told' means counted here, as in bank tellers: a priest tells the beads of the rosary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede, an eighth-century monk of Jarrow, wrote the Ecclesiastical History of the English People and was canonised.

clue.text: Fighter guillotined makes one jump

indicators.note: a guillotined thing has lost its head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a boxer is a fighter in the ring

explanation.surface: A combatant beheaded performs a single leap.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxer is a show-jumping fence made of a hedge with a rail, a single obstacle for horses.

clue.text: Loved piece involving early form of cycle (

indicators.note: involving can mean entangling or twisting together, so these letters are rolled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cherished item concerning an old-fashioned bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A velocipede is a nineteenth-century pedal-driven vehicle, precursor to the modern bicycle.

clue.text: Moderate politicians back a troubled state

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Wets was the label for moderate Conservatives who opposed Thatcher's hard line

explanation.surface: Moderate politicians are backing a country in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like 'support'; it is the reversal signal. Wets was 1980s slang for liberal-minded Tory ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being anxious or agitated, a flustered condition.

clue.text: Her sister should keep an eye on her

definitions.text: Her sister should keep an eye on her

blocks.clueFragment: Her sister should keep an eye on her
blocks.note: surface reading: an older sibling minding a younger girl
setter's reading: a hospital ward sister, senior to and supervising the nurses on her ward

explanation.surface: Family advice that a girl's sister ought to watch over her.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is the senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff nurse is a qualified hospital nurse ranking below the ward sister, who supervises her work.
